newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice futures close up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice futures close up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended up on Monday on institutional buying but trading was slow, with most retail investors staying on the sidelines, traders said.
The key September 1996 contract ended at 2,533 yuan ($305) per tonne, up six yuan. It opened at 2,534 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 2,531 and a high of 2,537.
October rose six yuan to 2,515 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 7,050 tonnes from 13,050.
Traders said many individual investors were sidelined today due to a lack of market-moving news and that institutional buying at low levels supported prices.
"Institutional buying was the main reason for today's rises but most individuals did not want to trade due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
Traders expect rice to consolidate at current levels in the next few days because of institutional support.
